subject: Clarifying monthly spend corridor and PO thresholds — OrchardML pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@orchardml.com>, Procurement Team <procure@orchardml.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-05T15:12:00Z
Subject: Clarifying monthly spend corridor and PO thresholds — OrchardML pilot

Hi Sam / Orchard procurement team,

Great to connect on the demo today — appreciate you walking through the burst profile. Quick recap and a few open items so your finance/procurement folks can move this to a PO: 

Summary of ask from call
- Target pilot size: 20M–60M tokens / month (expected median ~35M) based on 2–3 app workflows.
- Burst windows: short 2–3 hour bursts up to ~120M tokens/day on rare days — we discussed throttling/quotas to keep month spend predictable.
- Goal: procurement-friendly monthly commit (not an enterprise multi-year right away).

High-level pricing framing (placeholder numbers while I pull formal quote):
- Ballpark target you mentioned: ~$900–$1,100 per 1M tokens (you referenced an internal target of ~$1k/1M).
- For clarity: Redwood bills per actual token usage (prompt + completion + system tokens) unless you opt into prefix caching for highly repeated prompts.

Procurement thresholds we usually see and suggested alignment for OrchardML
- CC / small purchase: < $10k — simple card or low-touch agreement
- Standard PO lane: $10k–$50k — PO + standard MSSA (no custom SOW)
- Legal & SOW: > $50k — procurement + legal review, typical 1–2 week signoff window

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm expected committed monthly corridor (low / target / high) — e.g., 20 / 35 / 60M tokens?
2) Who is the AP contact and their PO minimum requirements (we saw a lot of variance across customers)?
3) Procurement: would Orchard accept a 30-day net PO for a $25k pilot, or do you require >$50k for standard PO lanes?

I've attached a draft quote (redwood-quote-orchardml-pilot-v2.pdf) and a short mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-orchardml.xlsx) that maps dates and owners for PO, legal, and onboarding.

If this is helpful I can propose a small three-line pricing tier (0–10M, 10–50M, 50M+) and slot our finance folks on a 15-minute call with your AP to speed the PO.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a revised quote once you confirm the corridor.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-quote-orchardml-pilot-v2.pdf (PDF), mutual-action-plan-orchardml.xlsx (Excel)

From: Sam Reynolds <sam@orchardml.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@orchardml.com>
Date: 2025-10-06T10:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying monthly spend corridor and PO thresholds — OrchardML pilot

Thanks Karthik — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token accounting: important for us — does the per-1M rate include both prompt and completion tokens? If there are cached prefixes, how does that change billing?

2) Band sensitivity: Our internal finance prefers seeing tiered pricing. Can you firm up illustrative $/1M token rates for three bands? We are thinking:
   - 0–10M
   - 10–50M
   - 50M+

3) Monthly band we should plan for: we’re comfortable committing to a 25–40M corridor for the pilot, but with a hard monthly cap option to avoid unexpected overage.

4) Procurement: we typically route POs through our AP person (cc’ed). Our internal threshold for small vendor PO signoff is $25k — anything above that triggers a manager approval. If Redwood can accept net-30 POs starting at $25k, that gets us moving.

Can your finance/legal come prepared with a W9 and the PO contact for AP? We’ll aim to convene our procurement manager Oct 10 and would appreciate a short (10–15m) call beforehand.

— Sam
Sam Reynolds
Head of Product, OrchardML
sam@orchardml.com

Thanks — a couple of procurement questions before we put the pilot PO on the calendar:
- Minimum PO amount you will accept as a signed vendor?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-06T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying monthly spend corridor and PO thresholds — OrchardML pilot

Hi Procurement / Sam — appreciate the quick turn. Answers inline and attached: 

1) Minimum PO: we can accept POs starting at $10k. For <$10k purchases we prefer credit card/stripe.

2) Vendor paperwork: attached redwood-W9.pdf and the standard MSSA link (DocuSign) — we can sign MSSA or accept a PO + our standard terms for pilots. If you need a counter-signed MSSA for >$50k we’ll route to legal.

3) Payment terms: net-30 is fine for pilot POs.

4) PO + SOW: for $25k–$50k pilots we can accept a PO without separate SOW — we include the service summary in the quote and onboarding sheet. Above $50k we recommend a short SOW to scope integration and SLA expectations.

Illustrative pricing tiers (final numbers will be on the attached quote PDF):
- 0–10M tokens / month: $1,200 per 1M tokens
- 10–50M tokens / month: $900 per 1M tokens
- 50M+ tokens / month: $700 per 1M tokens

Notes on billing: billing is per actual token usage (prompt + completion + system tokens). If you opt into prefix caching for frequently repeated prompts we can apply effective cost savings (reduced billable tokens for repeated inputs) — we can sketch that in the SOW if you want it formalized.

Attached: redwood-quote-orchardml-pilot-v2.pdf (revised with tiered pricing), redwood-W9.pdf, and the mutual action plan spreadsheet. I’ve also added a DocuSign MSSA link for quick signature: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-ORCHARD-ML

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Oct 6: Redwood sends updated quote & W9 (done)
- Oct 10: Orchard internal procurement approval meeting
- Oct 13: PO issued (target)
- Oct 15: Redwood receives PO & issues onboarding kickoff invite

If that timeline looks right I’ll have finance create a single-line PO-friendly quote and we’ll route to our AP contact as well.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
